question: What does the idiom 'To go for a song' mean?
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3** i.e. "Be sold cheaply".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"To go for a song"** means to be sold at a very low price or cheaply. (बहुत सस्ते में बिकना)
 
 
• **Example:** The antique vase went for a song at the auction because no one knew its true value.
 
 
• **"Be sold cheaply"** refers to something being sold at a price much lower than its actual worth. (सस्ते में बेचना)
 
 
• **Example:** Due to the urgent need for cash, he sold his car cheaply.
 
 
• Hence, the idiom "To go for a song" matches the meaning of "Be sold cheaply".

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3** i.e. "Be sold cheaply".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1: Be expensive** (महंगा होना): Refers to something that costs a lot of money.
 
 
• **Example:** The diamond necklace is very expensive and beyond my budget.
 
 
 
 
• **Option 2: Be unsold** (बिके बिना रह जाना): Refers to something that has not been purchased or bought.
 
 
• **Example:** Several products remained unsold at the end of the fair.
 
 
 
 
• **Option 4: Be sung loudly** (जोर से गाना): Refers to singing in a loud voice.
 
 
• **Example:** The choir sang the anthem loudly during the event.
